track: Track 2: The Agent That Can Explain Why
demo: local; see README Setup and Sample mode

sponsor_technology.zetaris: The five Acts are served from Zetaris as Lightning REST tables over pinned GitHub raw JSON, exposed as cached schema-store views (sections, acts, levies) that the Researcher queries with SQL; caching took a query from about 40 s to about 0.4 s.
sponsor_technology.meterless: Meterless Nightshift 1.2.3 is the primary AI provider for every product model call, with lane-pinned routing and a signed receipt on each call, and the H-MEM and World Model engines were implemented from the Meterless specs (conformance 7/7 and 8/8).
sponsor_technology.cursor: Cursor was used for edits during development; the organisers removed the Cursor requirement on 22 October.
sponsor_technology.nvidia: Both agents run on NVIDIA Nemotron through Nightshift, a fast 3.5 Lightning 30B Researcher and a 3 Ultra 550B Critic, and the per-call receipts record which model served each call.

development_tools: Claude Code (Anthropic), in the Claude Desktop app
Claude, for planning and prompt drafting

data_sources.title: Nigeria Tax Act, 2025
data_sources.copy: FGP gazette, NTA-2025-gazette-fgp.pdf (202 sections); the LIRS copy has 203 sections and is not cited

Taxes and Levies (Approved List for Collection) Act, 1998 (Cap. T2)
data_sources.copy: Nigeria_8_NigeriaTaxesLevies1998.pdf (5 sections, 1998 Schedule of 39 items only; not repealed by the 2025 Acts; the 2015 Amendment Order, set aside in 2020, is excluded; amounts are never asserted)

pre_existing_components: The Zetaris getting-started repository was read for SQL forms; nothing was copied from it.
The Meterless H-MEM and World Model engine specs are the design source; the engines were implemented from scratch.
Everything else was written during the hackathon.
